title: Kernel bundling + prefill-priority queue to mitigate FlashAttention v3 regression spikes
creator: Sanaa Patel
description: Investigate and implement a runtime-level kernel bundling strategy combined with a prefill-priority scheduling queue to reduce tail latency and OOM/regression incidents observed after enabling FlashAttention v3 on certain GPU sizes and sequence length distributions.
background: After the FlashAttention v3 rollout on ded-rt pools we observed intermittent latency and OOM spikes for mixed-batch workloads (long-short token mixes). The current kernel selector chooses v3 aggressively for medium/long sequences which, for some micro-tiling shapes and memory fragmentations, regresses p95/p99 and increases allocation churn. Prior work (ENG-33488, ENG-31765) focused on tiling heuristics and kernel scoring; this ticket explores a runtime 'bundle' approach plus a prefill queue to reduce kernel churn during prefill->decode transitions.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for representative echo+completion workload improves by >=10% versus current v3-enabled baseline on affected instance types
OOM incidents for the sampled fleet drop to zero in 48h canary window
No >5% throughput regression for short-only workloads in canary
Feature flag gated and config-driven: can be toggled per-pool and per-model
E2E QA run passing: correctness tests identical to baseline (no output divergence caused by scheduling)
implementation_notes: Add runtime kernel bundle abstraction: group compatible kernel variants (v2/v3/hybrid) into a candidate bundle at request admission time to minimize switching
Implement prefill-priority queue: prefill requests get scheduling preference to reserve KV slots and avoid interleaving decode requests that force kernel swaps
Heuristics for bundling: use batch token length histogram + estimated kv_cache_size to pick primary kernel, fallback order, and memory budget
Introduce 'bundle_age' TTL to allow periodic reevaluation for long-lived streams (avoid permanent bundling after model changes)
Expose configs via pool and model tags: runtime.pool.<pool>.kernel_bundle.enabled, runtime.model.<model>.prefer_v3_threshold
Add metrics: kernel_switch_count, bundle_hit_rate, prefill_wait_ms, prefill_priority_invocations
Add integration tests that simulate mixed-length batches and assert no kernel mismatch errors and stable memory usage
experiments: A/B canary on small slice of ded-rt-a GPUs: baseline v3-selector vs bundling+prefill (2:1 traffic)
Microbench harness: run token-level micro-bench across seq_lengths [32,128,512,1024] with variable batch mixes to map kernel switch heatmap
Stress test: long-lived multi-user prefill->decode sequences to measure bundle_age impact
Autotuner variant: add opt-in flag to autotuner to prefer v3 only when memory headroom > 12%
benchmark_results: Local perf harness (a100-40GB, mixed batch 16): baseline p95 73ms -> bundle+prefill p95 60ms (~18% improvement)
Canary run (ded-rt-a slice, 24h): OOMs dropped from 7 events to 0 on affected models, kernel_switch_count reduced by 42%
Short-only workload throughput drop measured at 2.4% (within target), p50 unchanged
Edge case: for seq=1024 heavy batches, v3 still outperforms; bundling must not force v2 for those cases
decisions: Primary: implement bundling at admission time rather than per-request to minimize selector calls and memory churn
Secondary: prefill requests get transient scheduling priority for up to 200ms or until KV reservation completes
Autotuner: add a threshold-based decision to prefer v3 when GPU free memory fraction > 12% and batch token variance < 0.35
Rollback: feature flag must support instant disable; rollback plan includes draining new bundles and forcing previous selector for 10s to clear in-flight streams
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bundling could overfit to admission snapshot and mis-handle later decode-heavy phases. Mitigation: bundle_age TTL and mid-stream reevaluation triggers on token distribution shift
Risk: Prefill priority could starve small decode requests. Mitigation: weighted-leaky-bucket that reserves 20% of slots for decode bursts
Risk: Incorrect heuristics might reduce v3 wins. Mitigation: extensive microbench and canary slices; default is opt-in for models in runtime.model.<model>.prefer_v3_threshold
Risk: Complexity increases scheduler maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep core logic <200 LOC; add comprehensive unit tests and observability
qa_plan: Unit tests for bundling logic covering histograms and fallback ordering
Integration tests with model-serving harness that reproduces mixed-length workloads
Regression test to assert identical decoded tokens across feature-flag toggles for 1000 synthetic prompts
Canary QA: 48h pass with p95 and OOM checks, then expand to 7d if stable
rollout_plan: Day 0: Merge behind feature flag and opt-in pool config; run integration tests in CI
Day 1: Canary on 1% traffic in ded-rt-a with 10 models that previously surfaced regressions
Day 3: Expand to 10% if canary metrics good (p95, OOM, kernel_switch_count), run additional stress tests
Day 7: Roll to 50% with monitoring and on-call guardrails, then full fleet after 7d stable
Immediate rollback criteria: p95 regresses >10% on canary, OOMs reappear, or kernel_switch_count doesn't reduce
